# Gemini on Mac Can Now Handle Repetitive Computer Chores: What It Does and Who It's For

> **In short:** Google has added computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, so Gemini can work through multi-step tasks across your local files, desktop apps, and websites. You describe the job, and Gemini does the clicking and typing while you stay in control. It's rolling out in English in the U.S.

Think about the tasks that eat up your afternoon: copying numbers from a PDF into a form, renaming a folder of photos, or pasting the same details into a spreadsheet for the fortieth time. Those jobs are dull, but they still need your attention. Google's new feature is aimed at exactly that kind of work.

## What "computer use" means

Computer use is the name for an AI that works the way you do on your computer. Instead of only answering questions in a chat window, it can move the cursor, click buttons, type text, and go through menus, much like a person would.

Google announced this for the Gemini app on Mac on November 19, 2026. According to Google, you can describe a workflow in plain language, and Gemini will handle the clicking, typing, and form entries from start to finish.

## How it works, in plain terms

Google describes a few features that make this feel less like handing over your keyboard:

- **A separate window:** Gemini works in its own isolated background window, with a live preview right in your chat. Your main screen and cursor stay free, so you can keep typing, designing, or taking a call.
- **Control over access:** You choose which apps Gemini is allowed to use.
- **Full visibility:** You can watch every step as it happens and pause at any time.
- **Approval for key actions:** Gemini asks you to approve important steps before they happen.

## Ideas for everyday use

Google lists a few examples of what people might try:

- **Batch editing photos:** Apply color grading to a set of images in your favorite design software.
- **Filling out forms:** Pull weights, dimensions, or addresses from local PDFs and enter them into a multi-box shipping quote.
- **Building a presentation:** Gather metrics and screenshots from dashboards and assemble them into a Google Slides deck.
- **Listing items for sale:** Review clothing photos in a folder, research prices, and prepare listings on resale sites.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: If you spend time on repeat tasks like sorting photos or moving details between files, this could save you real time. Start with a small, low-stakes job so you can see how Gemini handles it.
- **For your business or work**: Recurring reports, quote forms, and slide decks are natural candidates. Keep an eye on each step, since you will approve the important actions yourself.
- **If you're just getting started**: Try one task you already know well. Watching the live preview will teach you more than reading about it.
- **If you already use it**: Pair the feature with your own files. Ask Gemini to pull figures from a folder of PDFs and build a summary in Google Slides, then check each step in the live preview before you approve anything.

Some requirements apply. Google says the feature needs an Apple Silicon Mac (a Mac with Apple's own chip) running macOS Sequoia 15.0 or later. It's available for personal Google accounts aged 18 and older, and for Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra users. Check the official pricing page for plan details.

Google also announced a related tip for switching from another AI app. You can copy a prompt from Gemini's import settings, paste it into your previous AI tool to summarize your preferences, and paste that summary back into Gemini. You can also export your chat history as a ZIP file from your old provider and upload it in Gemini's settings.

## Wrap-up

Gemini's computer use feature is designed to handle the repetitive parts of your computer work while you focus on the rest. Google says you stay in charge through app permissions, live previews, and approvals. To get started, download the Gemini app for Mac at gemini.google/mac, and choose one small, repeatable task to test today.
